**My reasoning:**

I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My children moved to work in the city years ago, so it is mostly just me now. I cannot do what I used to do — my back gives me trouble and I tire easily. But I still know this land.

I will grow what I have always grown: **winter wheat** and **summer maize**, rotating on the same 8 mu. This is what makes sense here on the North China Plain. The soil knows these crops and I know them. Anything else would require me to learn new things at my age, and there is no good reason to take that risk.

After the wheat is harvested in June, I plant maize directly without plowing — my neighbor does the machine seeding for a small fee. I cannot operate the heavy tiller myself anymore. For wheat in October, I hire rotary tillage before planting.

For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer as a base when planting wheat, then urea as a topdressing before jointing in spring. For maize, I apply urea once at the big bell stage. These amounts are what I've used for years and the yields have been acceptable.

Irrigation: I pump from the village well. Wheat needs water at wintering, jointing, and heading — three times. Maize I usually only need to water once if the summer rains are decent. Electricity for pumping costs money, so I try not to over-irrigate.

I buy seeds from the village supply cooperative. Improved wheat variety, hybrid maize — that is what everyone uses now and the yields are reliable.

I spray herbicide before wheat emergence and fungicide once in spring. For maize I spray for corn borer if I see damage.
